To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method of shape analysis for classification of masses based upon their boundaries which can be used to distinguish between benign and malignant tumours and also to classify circumscribed masses and spiculated masses.
the proposed method of shape analysis of the mammographic masses is based on the local shape features and it can be used to classify circumscribed and spiculated masses with high accuracy.

the combination of SI and fcc resulted in an improved classification of benign and malign masses, with an area (A(z)) under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve of 0.81, and that the combination of all three features (compactness, SI, and fcc) resulted in a classification of spiculated versus circumscribed masses with A(z) of 0 91.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for boundary segmentation and shape analysis of masses.
shape features of masses that are localised in the boundary and that may not be detected by global shape analysis methods.
developing new shape analysis methods for the classification of mammographic lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of local shape features in combination with global shape features can be a useful approach for the classification of masses.

the use of the proposed shape features, SI and fcc, in conjunction with other shape features, such as compactness, can improve the accuracy of benign/malignant and circumscribed/spiculated classification of mammographic tumours.
the proposed methods of shape feature analysis based on local details of the boundary of the object can be used for computer-aided diagnosis of mammographic masses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shape analysis of masses based on boundary modelling methods can provide a useful tool to assist radiologists in the classification of mammographic tumours.
the proposed methods of shape modelling of the boundaries of breast masses have resulted in an improvement in classification performance of benign and malignant tumours.
the proposed shape analysis methods are able to classify the shape of mammographic masses correctly and are able to identify exceptions in the shape of benign and malignant masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of local and global shape features can be used for classification of benign and spiculated masses with high accuracy and can also provide a better insight into the shape of masses than the global shape analysis methods.
the shape of masses can be analysed in terms of concavity fraction and spiculation index, which is useful in classification of benign and malign masses.
shape features based on boundary modelling can be used to improve the classification accuracy of masses.
